Frozencontract.

CONTRACT.md freezes the RKV1 container, events, verdicts, canonical outputs, the scheduler model and determinism. Changing any of it is an explicit PR.

  1. C11Pure corecore/ has no fopen, clock, socket, allocation or QNX header — buffers come from the caller.
  2. PyIndependent twinhost/ is stdlib-only Python. Freezing a scenario refuses to write if C and Python disagree.
  3. ≠No wrong replayUnmodelled policies are reported (sporadic-not-modelled), never replayed wrong.

Shown exactly as the repo writes it. The limits are part of the product.

TrialQuestionStatus — PREUVE.md §3Note
E1.kev format documentedVerifiedsys/trace.h + traceprinter oracle
E2tracelogger freezes cleanly, pre-crash history keptNot verifiedtable says so; r630 notes report a freeze — repo inconsistent
E3process termination observable in real timeNot verifiedHAM gone in QNX 8 → /proc polling
E4scheduler model faithful to QNXPartialP2 holds on fixtures; model is a subset
E5dumper core holds thread statesNot verifiedCORRELATION_OK never emitted yet
  1. No wait-for graph on the REAL trace: QNX 8.0 does not expose the sync-object id (the mutex goes through a MsgSend whose body is not traced). No DEADLOCK_FOUND is claimed there.
  2. SCHED_SPORADIC and adaptive partitions are not modelled — replay reports sporadic-not-modelled, never a wrong replay.
  3. The demo guest records in "fast" mode: the faulty process is only captured by the separate "wide" trace.
  4. R1–R5 are absence claims about public QNX docs, to re-check page by page (docs/GAP.md).
  5. No GitHub Pages site for the repo; no demo-video URL found in the repo (unknown).

Next: the wait-for graphon message channels.

The real trace exposes each send's rcvid channel and its owner pid — rebuilding the graph on channels instead of mutexes is the natural next step (docs/PREUVE.md). Codelab: 4 chapters — freeze, explain, replay, go further.
